title: Using and understanding a Chromatograms object
text: package provides four imputation methods: “linear”: Linear interpolation known values. Fast simple, good data regular gaps. “spline”: Cubic spline interpolation. Provides smooth curves may introduce artifacts. “gaussian”: Gaussian kernel smoothing. Uses Gaussian kernel estimate values based neighboring points. “loess”: Locally weighted scatter plot smoothing. Provides robust smoothing local polynomial regression.

text: compareChromatograms() function computes pairwise similarity chromatograms two steps. First, mapping function (MAPFUN, default matchRtime()) aligns two chromatograms onto common retention-time grid linear interpolation, returning aligned intensity vectors . , scoring function (FUN, default cor(), .e. Pearson correlation) computes similarity value vectors. Additional arguments method = "spearman" can passed via ... scoring function, fully custom FUN MAPFUN can supplied. result always 3-dimensional numeric array dimensions n × m × 2. Layer [, , "score"] contains pairwise similarity scores; layer [, , "n_peaks"] contains number overlapping retention-time points used comparison. minPeaks parameter (default 4) sets minimum number overlapping points required compute score — pairs threshold return NA score layer actual overlap count still recorded n_peaks. avoids unreliable scores sparse overlaps skips FUN computation entirely pairs. Use minPeaks = 2L compute score whenever two points overlap.
